job.title: Platform Manager- Salesforce
job.html_description:
Description


U.S. Soccer Overview


The U.S. Soccer Federation exists in service to soccer. Our aim is to ignite a national passion for the game. Because we believe that soccer is more than a sport; it is a force for good.


We understand the importance and the power of teamwork, on and off the pitch. That is why we work closely with our Federation partners and members, to inspire, support and guide every level of the game: from the grassroots to the National Teams. We want to bring soccer into every home and every community, right across America. Because we believe that soccer can transform lives like no other sport. Soccer can represent the best of U.S.


U.S. Soccer is in a period of significant growth, with ambitious plans for U.S. Soccer in the near and far future. We are, therefore, looking for dynamic servant leaders to join us on this journey: in service to soccer. Applicants must be able to demonstrate visionary leadership, analytical decision-making, professional flexibility, and an empathic management style that builds bold teams and delivers globally significant results.


Position Description


The U.S. Soccer Federation seeks a Salesforce Platform Manager to own project management and translate business requirements into epics and user stories. This role ensures that Salesforce becomes the trusted CRM platform for broad Federation use. The Manager must bring experience in philanthropy and CRM adoption for small-to-medium non-profit organizations, with an ability to scale to a national platform. The role requires balancing platform governance with business needs. This position reports to the Senior Salesforce Administrator.


Primary Responsibilities

  • Act as a product manager for Salesforce: manage the platform roadmap, prioritize enhancements, and oversee backlog grooming.
  • Facilitate Agile ceremonies in JIRA including sprint planning, stand-ups, retrospectives, and reviews to ensure timely delivery of value.
  • Translate diverse business requirements into epics, user stories, and acceptance criteria with clear definitions of success.
  • Partner with advancement, finance, and program teams to understand business processes and optimize Salesforce to support holistic customer relationship management.
  • Oversee end-to-end project management for Salesforce initiatives, including defining scope, setting timelines, coordinating cross-functional stakeholders, and ensuring on-time delivery aligned with business objectives
  • Coordinate with Salesforce administrators, developers, and external partners/vendors to deliver platform solutions and integrations
  • Develop and maintain governance processes for data integrity, user adoption, and change management.
  • Serve as the bridge between technical teams and business stakeholders, ensuring platform solutions are user-centered and mission-driven.

Requirements

 

Minimum Qualifications 

  • 3+ years of professional experience managing Salesforce as a platform in a nonprofit or fundraising environment.
  • Proven track record acting as a product owner/manager: backlog management, sprint planning, and Agile delivery
  • Familiarity with fundraising operations, donor engagement, campaign tracking, and grant management processes
  • Strong collaboration and relationship-building abilities across teams and functions
  • General knowledge of soccer
  • Capable of working in fast-paced and demanding environments
  • Proficient experience with Microsoft Suite (Word, PowerPoint, Excel, and Outlook)
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
  • Must be able to connect “micro” details to the “macro” vision and mission.

Desired Qualifications

  • Demonstrated strategic hustle and work ethic with diversity of thought
  • A background in, and passion for, soccer, sports and/or entertainment is preferred
  • Ability to handle multiple projects, tasks, and priorities
  • Bilingual (English and Spanish, preferred)
  • Collaborative, team-player with a results-driven mindset
  • Strong problem-solving capabilities to address and resolve issues that face a growing company
  • Proven ability to set and deliver on clear, ambitious goals and to be accountable for results
  • Creative thinker, self-starter with strong analytical skills


U.S. Soccer offers a comprehensive compensation package, casual work environment, an inclusive culture, and an atmosphere for professional development.


U.S. Soccer is an equal opportunity employer that is committed to diversity, equity, and inclusion, and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any kind on the basis of race, color, sex, religion, national origin, citizenship, pregnancy, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, disability, genetic information, military status, political belief, or any other characteristic protected under the law. This policy applies to all our employment practices within our organization. We strongly encourage women, people of color, LGBTQIA, veterans, parents, and persons with disabilities to apply.

job.title: Nike Performance Innovation Lead
job.html_description:
Description


Position Description


Nike is seeking an applied research and innovation specialist with a strong foundation in sport science and experience working in elite high-performance environments to consult in the newly created Performance Innovation Lab at the National Training Center in Fayetteville, Georgia. The ideal candidate will combine scientific thinking with practical delivery, contributing to applied research initiatives while supporting the development and operation of the Performance Innovation Lab at US Soccer’s Arthur M. Blank National Training Center, as well as other Nike initiatives and sponsored athletes. Funded in partnership with Nike, Inc., this initiative is designed to advance the science and practice of elite soccer performance across all 27-U.S. Soccer National Teams—from youth development through senior international competition.  


This role sits at the intersection of elite applied sport science and rigorous research, and given its location, will be embedded within U.S. Soccer’s daily operations while maintaining a strategic research agenda that generates new knowledge for the federation, its athletes, and the broader U.S.  soccer ecosystem. As a Nike position, the role will also support select non-soccer Nike initiatives and athletes who access the facility and Performance Innovation Lab, creating cross-sport research opportunities.  


Employment Notice 


This position is contracted by Nike, Inc. Although posted on U.S. Soccer's career site and based at the U.S. Soccer Arthur M. Blank National Training Center, the successful candidate will be contracted solely by Nike and will be subject to Nike's code of conduct and handbook. Collaboration with and day-to-day direction from U.S. Soccer personnel does not create an employment, joint employment, agency, or contractual relationship with U.S. Soccer, which assumes no liability for employment-related matters associated with this role. By submitting an application for this position, applicants acknowledge that this will be a one year contracted role with potential for extension and that they have read and understand this Employment Notice.


Primary Responsibilities


This role will operate across two interconnected domains: 


 Applied Research

  • Support the design and execution of applied research projects aligned with performance priorities, including data collection, analysis, and interpretation 
  • Develop and maintain a multi-year research agenda aligned with federation performance priorities and Nike’s innovation interests 
  • Build longitudinal datasets—including biomechanical profiles—spanning youth through senior levels across men’s and women’s programs 
  • Identify cross-team performance patterns, developmental benchmarks, and evidence-based recommendations for coaching and performance staff 
  • Pursue external collaborations with universities, research institutions, and sport science organizations to extend the reach and rigor of the research program 
  • Present findings to internal stakeholders, at professional conferences, and through peer reviewed publication 

Practitioner Services

  • Deliver biomechanical and performance science assessments to National Teams during training camps and residencies at the Arthur M. Blank National Training Center 
  • Develop standardized assessment protocols and normative databases that can be administered across all 27 teams, including by other qualified staff 
  • Support Integrated Performance Support and Sporting staff by providing evidence-informed insights contributing to training, loading, recovery, and performance optimization decisions 
  • Support select Nike-sponsored athletes from other sports who access the lab and campus, facilitating cross-sport data collection and innovation 
  • Female 360: Contribute expertise to the design and delivery of U.S. Soccer's Female 360 health assessments and initiatives, supporting a holistic, athlete-centered approach to women's health and performance 
  • Contribute to the development of a scalable service model delivered through the Performance Innovation Lab (e.g., testing, profiling, applied workshops, educational visits) 
  • Translate research insights into practical, actionable tools and recommendations for coaching and performance staff 

Lab & Campus Innovation 

  • Support the procurement, commissioning, and ongoing execution of projects at the Performance Innovation Lab at the US Soccer Arthur M. Blank National Training Center 
  • Drive the “campus-as-lab” vision: identify opportunities to instrument training environments, integrate technology into daily operations, and turn routine activities into data collection opportunities 
  • Evaluate emerging technologies, methodologies, and tools for potential integration into the lab and broader campus infrastructure 
  • Establish data governance, quality assurance, and athlete data privacy protocols for all research and assessment activities

Requirements


Minimum Qualifications

  • Doctoral degree (PhD or equivalent) in Sport Science, Kinesiology, Biomechanics, Human Movement Science, Sport Physiology, or a closely related discipline 
  • Minimum of 8 years of combined experience in applied sport science research and elite sport performance support, including at least 3 years in a high-performance sport environment (e.g., professional club, national federation, institute of sport) 
  • Experience working across both men’s and women’s sport programs 
  • Demonstrated expertise in biomechanical assessment methodologies, including experience with force platforms, 3D motion capture, inertial measurement units, and/or pressure mapping systems 
  • A peer-reviewed publication record that reflects both scientific rigor and applied relevance 
  •  Experience designing and managing multi-site or multi-team research projects 
  • Strong interpersonal and communication skills, with a demonstrated ability to translate complex scientific concepts for coaches, medical staff, and organizational leadership 
  • Ability to operate independently with minimal supervision while navigating a complex, multistakeholder organizational environment

Preferred Qualifications 

  • Experience in elite football/soccer environments at the club or international level  
  • Familiarity with the demands and structures of national team programs, including athlete availability constraints and multi-team coordination 
  • Experience with longitudinal athlete monitoring and developmental tracking across age groups 
  • Experience working with advanced soccer tracking technologies, including player surface interaction technology, is considered a strong advantage 
  • Background in or exposure to sport technology innovation, product development, or industry academic partnerships 
  • Proficiency with data management platforms, statistical software, and visualization tools used in applied sport science

What This Role Offers 

  • A newly created role within a new, strategically significant initiative backed by both the U.S. Soccer Federation and Nike, Inc. 
  •  Access to a purpose-built Performance Innovation Lab at a world-class National Training Center 
  • Unparalleled population access: 27 National Teams spanning youth through senior, men’s and women’s, all operating from a centralized campus 
  • The opportunity to build longitudinal datasets and research programs that have no existing equivalent in world football 
  • A platform for high-impact publication, professional visibility, and thought leadership in sport science 
  • Cross-sport exposure through Nike’s broader athlete network and innovation ecosystem 

Key Relationships


The role maintains collaborative working relationships with National Team Integrated Performance, support staff, Nike’s Sport Research Lab (NSRL) and innovation teams, and external academic and research partners. 

 

Governance & Accountability


The role reports into the Nike’s NSRL Team in Beaverton, OR and U.S. Soccer’s Performance  Innovation Team in Fayetteville, GA. U.S. Soccer research priorities are set collaboratively between U.S. Soccer leadership and Nike, with a defined engagement cadence (e.g., quarterly research updates, annual innovation reviews). The role holder is expected to maintain scientific independence and ethical standards in all research activities. 


Day-to-day project priorities may be coordinated with designated U.S. Soccer personnel; however, Nike retains sole responsibility for all contract-related matters. Nothing in this reporting or collaborative structure shall be interpreted as creating an employment relationship between the employee and U.S. Soccer.


To Apply


Interested candidates should submit a curriculum vitae, a cover letter addressing their vision for the role, and the names of three professional references. Review of applications will begin immediately and continue until the position is filled.


Nike is an equal opportunity employer and values diversity in its workforce.

job.title: Director, Performance Nutrition
job.html_description:
Description


U.S. Soccer Overview


The U.S. Soccer Federation exists in service to soccer. Our aim is to ignite a national passion for the game. Because we believe that soccer is more than a sport; it is a force for good.


We understand the importance and the power of teamwork, on and off the pitch. That is why we work closely with our Federation partners and members, to inspire, support and guide every level of the game: from the grassroots to the National Teams. We want to bring soccer into every home and every community, right across America. Because we believe that soccer can transform lives like no other sport. Soccer can represent the best of U.S.


U.S. Soccer is in a period of significant growth, with ambitious plans for U.S. Soccer in the near and far future. We are, therefore, looking for dynamic servant leaders to join us on this journey: in service to soccer. Applicants must be able to demonstrate visionary leadership, analytical decision-making, professional flexibility, and an empathic management style that builds bold teams and delivers globally significant results.


Position Description


U.S. Soccer is seeking an innovative and collaborative leader to serve as the Director of Performance Nutrition. As a senior leader within the Integrated Performance Support (IPS) Unit, this role will oversee the strategic vision, operational delivery, and continued evolution of performance nutrition and culinary services across the Federation’s National Team environments.


Working within a cross-functional team, this position will collaborate across Performance Medicine, Performance Science, Performance & Data Analytics, and Performance Innovation to support player development, health, performance, and longevity.


The Director will guide an integrated model that combines world-class performance nutrition, culinary operations, player and coach education, body composition strategy, recovery fueling, and performance dining experiences to support elite preparation and sustained high performance.


Working closely with the Executive Director of Culinary Services at the Arthur M. Blank National Training Center, National Team Performance Chefs, consulting sports dietitians, and IPS practitioners, this individual will build scalable systems and standards that elevate athlete care and performance support across Youth, Extended, and Senior National Team programs.


The ideal candidate is a progressive systems thinker and relationship-builder who thrives in collaborative, fast-paced, high-performance environments, brings a team-first mindset, and a passion for innovation.


Primary Responsibilities

  

Leadership, Culinary Operations & Network Management

  • Lead and oversee U.S. Soccer’s Performance Nutrition & Culinary Services strategy across all National Team programs and events
  • Direct and support a growing network that includes:
    • National Training Center Executive Chef
    • Full-time Performance Chef staff
    • Consulting and network sports dietitians
    • External nutrition partners (i.e.: Powerade)
  • Establish operational standards, workflows, service expectations, and performance systems across all nutrition and culinary environments
  • Collaborate with culinary leadership to deliver elite dining and fueling experiences at the National Training Center and during camps, competitions, and travel
  • Develop scalable systems for menu planning, supplementation, hydration delivery, grab-and-go fueling, recovery stations, and performance dining operations
  • Oversee vendor relationships, food sourcing strategies, inventory systems, budget planning, and quality assurance processes
  • Create alignment and continuity across Youth & Extended National Team environments through centralized standards 
  • Build and support a high-performance culture centered on collaboration, innovation, learning, mentorship, and athlete service

Athlete Profiling, Fueling & Readiness Strategy

  • Lead U.S. Soccer’s fueling optimization strategy 
  • Design and operationalize evidence-informed nutrition systems that maximize availability, adaptation, recovery, resilience, and long-term athlete health
  • Lead body composition and athlete profiling initiatives in collaboration with Performance Science, Performance Medicine, and Performance & Data Analytics staff
  • Establish federation-wide standards and best practices for body composition assessment, interpretation, reporting, and education
  • Integrate body composition insights into individualized nutrition periodization, recovery planning, readiness management, and long-term athlete development strategies
  • Support growth and maturation considerations within Youth National Team environments through integrated monitoring and education systems
  • Collaborate across IPS to support integrated performance planning and real-time readiness management processes
  • Utilize data-informed approaches to optimize fueling, hydration, recovery, and player availability strategies

Integrated Performance Collaboration

  • Operate as a senior leader within a transdisciplinary Integrated Performance Support model built around shared accountability and collaborative decision-making
  • Contribute to athlete profiling and long-term player development systems
  • Partner with Performance Innovation and Data Analytics to evolve monitoring systems, education tools, and performance nutrition technologies
  • Support integrated performance planning processes that align technical, tactical, physical, psychosocial and nutritional priorities into one unified preparation strategy
  • Collaborate with clubs, external providers, and federation stakeholders to ensure continuity and alignment of athlete support systems
  • Contribute to the continued evolution of U.S. Soccer’s high-performance environments and athlete experience standards

Requirements


Minimum Qualifications

  • Master’s degree in Nutrition, Dietetics, Exercise Science, or related field required; PhD preferred
  • Registered Dietitian (RD/RDN) in good standing with applicable state licensure
  • Board Certified Specialist in Sports Dietetics (CSSD)
  • ISAK Level 1 (or higher) accreditation
  • Minimum 8 years of experience in elite sport, professional sport, collegiate athletics, Olympic sport, or federation environments
  • Demonstrated experience leading integrated performance nutrition programs and/or culinary performance operations
  • Experience managing interdisciplinary staff, consultants, vendors, or distributed service networks
  • Strong applied expertise in body composition assessment, athlete profiling, nutrition periodization, and performance fueling strategies within elite sport environments
  • Experience collaborating within interdisciplinary performance and medical teams
  • Knowledge of WADA, USADA, FIFA, and anti-doping best practices related to supplementation and athlete education
  • Strong operational leadership, communication, organizational, and project management skills
  • Capable of working in fast-paced and demanding environments
  • Must be able to connect “micro” details to the “macro” vision and mission
  • Proficient experience with Microsoft Suite (Word, PowerPoint, Excel, and Outlook)
  • Ability to work non-traditional hours, including evenings, weekends, and extensive domestic/international travel


Desired Qualifications

  • Previous experience within professional sport, Olympic sport, and National Team environments is desired


U.S. Soccer offers a comprehensive compensation package, casual work environment, an inclusive culture, and an atmosphere for professional development.


U.S. Soccer is an equal opportunity employer that is committed to diversity, equity, and inclusion, and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any kind on the basis of race, color, sex, religion, national origin, citizenship, pregnancy, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, disability, genetic information, military status, political belief, or any other characteristic protected under the law. This policy applies to all our employment practices within our organization. We strongly encourage women, people of color, LGBTQIA, veterans, parents, and persons with disabilities to apply.

job.title: Senior Performance Therapist
job.html_description:
Description


U.S. Soccer Overview


The U.S. Soccer Federation exists in service to soccer. Our aim is to ignite a national passion for the game. Because we believe that soccer is more than a sport; it is a force for good.


We understand the importance and the power of teamwork, on and off the pitch. That is why we work closely with our Federation partners and members, to inspire, support and guide every level of the game: from the grassroots to the National Teams. We want to bring soccer into every home and every community, right across America. Because we believe that soccer can transform lives like no other sport. Soccer can represent the best of U.S.


U.S. Soccer is in a period of significant growth, with ambitious plans for U.S. Soccer in the near and far future. We are, therefore, looking for dynamic servant leaders to join us on this journey: in service to soccer. Applicants must be able to demonstrate visionary leadership, analytical decision-making, professional flexibility, and an empathic management style that builds bold teams and delivers globally significant results.


Position Description


The Senior Performance Therapist is a leader within U.S. Soccer's Integrated Performance Support (IPS) department, supporting Youth and Extended National Teams and advancing an integrated model of development, health & wellbeing, and performance.


This role is responsible for delivering world-class performance physical therapy services while leading the design and implementation of criteria-based return-to-performance (RTP) systems, supporting longitudinal athlete health strategies, and integrating performance medicine with performance science, strength & conditioning, performance nutrition, analytics, and innovation.


The Senior Performance Therapist will play a critical role in developing scalable systems and best practices for the National Training Center, ensuring that athlete care is collaborative, data-informed, and aligned with U.S. Soccer's long-term player development philosophy.


In addition to direct athlete care, this position will mentor staff, contribute to interdisciplinary decision-making, and help establish Integrated Performance Support as a world-class model for performance preservation, and continuous innovation.


Primary Responsibilities

  

Performance Therapy & Athlete Care

  • Deliver comprehensive performance therapy services across Youth National Team and Extended National Team camps, training environments, and competitions.
  • Lead injury assessment, manual therapy interventions, rehabilitation/reconditioning planning, and progressive return-to-performance programming.
  • Develop and implement individualized injury prevention and movement optimization strategies.
  • Collaborate with Integrated Performance Support staff to optimize athlete readiness, availability, and long-term development.
  • Support continuity of care across club and national team environments.

Return-to-Performance Leadership

  • Lead the design, implementation, and continuous refinement of criteria-based return-to-performance (RTP) frameworks.
  • Establish standardized rehabilitation and RTP processes across Youth National Team environments.
  • Integrate objective testing, movement quality, strength diagnostics, load tolerance, and athlete readiness into RTP decision-making.
  • Develop decision-making frameworks that promote consistency, transparency, and athlete-centered progression.
  • Continuously evaluate and improve RTP systems using current evidence and organizational data.

Integrated Performance Support Leadership

  • Serve as a collaborative leader within the Integrated Performance Support (IPS) department.
  • Foster interdisciplinary collaboration across performance medicine, performance science, strength & conditioning, performance nutrition, analytics, coaching, and innovation.
  • Develop shared mental models, communication standards, and integrated decision-making processes that improve athlete care.
  • Contribute to the development of scalable systems and best practices that support all National Team environments.
  • Champion a culture of collaboration, curiosity, accountability, and continuous improvement.

Performance Science Integration & Innovation

  • Integrate performance science into daily clinical practice and reconditioning planning.
  • Utilize the VALD performance technology suite and other athlete monitoring systems to inform reconditioning progressions and return-to-performance decisions.
  • Translate force, movement, neuromuscular, and load data into actionable clinical interventions.
  • Partner with Performance Science staff to develop testing protocols, athlete profiling strategies, and evidence-informed practices.
  • Support innovation initiatives that improve athlete care, decision-making, and organizational capability.

Longitudinal Athlete Health & Analytics

  • Support longitudinal injury surveillance and availability tracking.
  • Analyze injury trends, recurrence rates, workload patterns, and availability metrics to identify opportunities for improvement.
  • Develop reporting and insights that inform integrated planning and athlete management.
  • Support long-term athlete development through data-informed recommendations and proactive intervention strategies.

Leadership & Staff Development

  • Mentor and develop therapists, athletic trainers, interns, and other clinical support staff.
  • Foster interdisciplinary learning and knowledge sharing across the department.
  • Support onboarding, education, and professional development initiatives.
  • Contribute to building a high-performing team culture grounded in teamwork, innovation, and continuous improvement.

Requirements


Minimum Qualifications

  • Licensed Physical Therapist (PT) with active Georgia licensure or ability to obtain licensure prior to employment.
  • Elite sport experience required, including professional, Olympic, academy, or national team environments.
  • Demonstrated expertise in:
    • Rehabilitation and soccer-specific return-to-performance programming
    • Criteria-based RTP system design and implementation
    • Evidence-informed diagnostics, injury prevention and load management strategies
    • Manual therapy and therapeutic exercise and prescription
  • Strong experience integrating performance science into clinical decision-making.
  • Working knowledge of the VALD performance technology suite (ForceDecks, ForceFrame, Dynamo, SmartSpeed, HumanTrak or similar technologies) and the ability to translate objective performance data into athlete care strategies.
  • Experience working within multidisciplinary Integrated Performance environments.
  • Capable of working in fast-paced and demanding environments.
  • Must be able to connect “micro” details to the “macro” vision and mission.
  • Proficient experience with Microsoft Suite (Word, PowerPoint, Excel, and Outlook).


Desired Qualifications

Position Description
The Senior Performance Therapist is a leader within U.S. Soccer's Integrated Performance Support (IPS) department, supporting Youth and Extended National Teams and advancing an integrated model of development, health & wellbeing, and performance.
This role is responsible for delivering world-class performance physical therapy services while leading the design and implementation of criteria-based return-to-performance (RTP) systems, supporting longitudinal athlete health strategies, and integrating performance medicine with performance science, strength & conditioning, performance nutrition, analytics, and innovation.
The Senior Performance Therapist will play a critical role in developing scalable systems and best practices for the National Training Center, ensuring that athlete care is collaborative, data-informed, and aligned with U.S. Soccer's long-term player development philosophy.
In addition to direct athlete care, this position will mentor staff, contribute to interdisciplinary decision-making, and help establish Integrated Performance Support as a world-class model for performance preservation, and continuous innovation.
Primary Responsibilities
Performance Therapy & Athlete Care
- Deliver comprehensive performance therapy services across Youth National Team and Extended National Team camps, training environments, and competitions. - Lead injury assessment, manual therapy interventions, rehabilitation/reconditioning planning, and progressive return-to-performance programming. - Develop and implement individualized injury prevention and movement optimization strategies. - Collaborate with Integrated Performance Support staff to optimize athlete readiness, availability, and long-term development. - Support continuity of care across club and national team environments.
Return-to-Performance Leadership
- Lead the design, implementation, and continuous refinement of criteria-based return-to-performance (RTP) frameworks. - Establish standardized rehabilitation and RTP processes across Youth National Team environments. - Integrate objective testing, movement quality, strength diagnostics, load tolerance, and athlete readiness into RTP decision-making. - Develop decision-making frameworks that promote consistency, transparency, and athlete-centered progression. - Continuously evaluate and improve RTP systems using current evidence and organizational data.
Integrated Performance Support Leadership
- Serve as a collaborative leader within the Integrated Performance Support (IPS) department. - Foster interdisciplinary collaboration across performance medicine, performance science, strength & conditioning, performance nutrition, analytics, coaching, and innovation. - Develop shared mental models, communication standards, and integrated decision-making processes that improve athlete care. - Contribute to the development of scalable systems and best practices that support all National Team environments. - Champion a culture of collaboration, curiosity, accountability, and continuous improvement.
Performance Science Integration & Innovation
- Integrate performance science into daily clinical practice and reconditioning planning. - Utilize the VALD performance technology suite and other athlete monitoring systems to inform reconditioning progressions and return-to-performance decisions. - Translate force, movement, neuromuscular, and load data into actionable clinical interventions. - Partner with Performance Science staff to develop testing protocols, athlete profiling strategies, and evidence-informed practices. - Support innovation initiatives that improve athlete care, decision-making, and organizational capability.
Longitudinal Athlete Health & Analytics
- Support longitudinal injury surveillance and availability tracking. - Analyze injury trends, recurrence rates, workload patterns, and availability metrics to identify opportunities for improvement. - Develop reporting and insights that inform integrated planning and athlete management. - Support long-term athlete development through data-informed recommendations and proactive intervention strategies.
Leadership & Staff Development
- Mentor and develop therapists, athletic trainers, interns, and other clinical support staff. - Foster interdisciplinary learning and knowledge sharing across the department. - Support onboarding, education, and professional development initiatives. - Contribute to building a high-performing team culture grounded in teamwork, innovation, and continuous improvement.

Minimum Qualifications
- Licensed Physical Therapist (PT) with active Georgia licensure or ability to obtain licensure prior to employment. - Elite sport experience required, including professional, Olympic, academy, or national team environments. - Demonstrated expertise in: Rehabilitation and soccer-specific return-to-performance programming Criteria-based RTP system design and implementation Evidence-informed diagnostics, injury prevention and load management strategies Manual therapy and therapeutic exercise and prescription - Strong experience integrating performance science into clinical decision-making. - Working knowledge of the VALD performance technology suite (ForceDecks, ForceFrame, Dynamo, SmartSpeed, HumanTrak or similar technologies) and the ability to translate objective performance data into athlete care strategies. - Experience working within multidisciplinary Integrated Performance environments. - Capable of working in fast-paced and demanding environments. - Must be able to connect “micro” details to the “macro” vision and mission. - Proficient experience with Microsoft Suite (Word, PowerPoint, Excel, and Outlook).
Desired Qualifications
- Experience supporting elite soccer athletes within professional clubs, academies, or national team environments. - Experience working with youth elite athletes and an understanding of growth, maturation, and long-term athlete development principles. - Experience designing systems, processes, and operating standards across multiple teams or performance environments.

job.title: VALD Performance Science Fellowship
job.html_description:
Description


U.S. Soccer Overview

  

The U.S. Soccer Federation exists in service to soccer. Our aim is to ignite a national passion for the game. Because we believe that soccer is more than a sport; it is a force for good.


We understand the importance and the power of teamwork, on and off the pitch. That is why we work closely with our Federation partners and members, to inspire, support and guide every level of the game: from the grassroots to the National Teams. We want to bring soccer into every home and every community, right across America. Because we believe that soccer can transform lives like no other sport. Soccer can represent the best of U.S.


U.S. Soccer is in a period of significant growth, with ambitious plans for U.S. Soccer in the near and far future. We are, therefore, looking for dynamic servant leaders to join us on this journey: in service to soccer. Applicants must be able to demonstrate visionary leadership, analytical decision-making, professional flexibility, and an empathic management style that builds bold teams and delivers globally significant results.


Position Description 


The United States Soccer Federation (USSF) is launching the inaugural Performance Science Fellowship, a unique one-year development opportunity designed to prepare the next generation of high-performance practitioners.


Funded through a strategic collaboration with VALD, one of the world's leading sports science and human performance technology companies, this fellowship provides unparalleled exposure to elite athlete preparation, applied research, data analytics, innovation, and integrated performance support.


Based at the new National Training Center (NTC), the fellow will work across Youth National Teams, Extended National Teams, Coach Education, and Performance Innovation initiatives while collaborating with practitioners in performance medicine, strength & conditioning, performance science, performance nutrition, analytics and innovation.


This position is designed for an early-career practitioner who wants to bridge the gap between academic performance science and applied high-performance sport.


Fellowship Objectives


The Performance Science Fellow will:

  • Support the delivery of an integrated performance support model across the National Training Center 
  • Translate performance data into actionable insights for coaches and practitioners 
  • Assist with athlete testing, monitoring, and reporting using industry-leading technologies 
  • Contribute to research, innovation, and knowledge sharing initiatives 
  • Develop expertise in applied sports science within an elite international sporting environment 

The fellowship is intended to create future leaders who combine scientific rigor with practical impact.


Primary Responsibilities


Performance Science & Athlete Monitoring

  • Support athlete profiling, testing, and monitoring across National Team programs 
  • Assist with force, strength, wellness, and movement assessments utilizing VALD technologies and other performance systems 
  • Prepare performance dashboards and reports for multidisciplinary staff 
  • Help maintain data quality, integrity, and longitudinal athlete records 
  • Integrated Performance Support
  • Work collaboratively with practitioners across pe literature reviews and evidence synthesis 
  • Translate emerging research into practical recommendations for coaches and staff 

Education & Knowledge Sharing

  • The fellow will play an active role in advancing practitioner education by supporting initiatives such as performance science presentations, internal learning sessions, National Training Center educational events, practitioner workshops and digital educational content and articles 

Technology & Data

  • Develop practical expertise using VALD HumanTrak, ForceDecks, ForceFrame, SmartSpeed, Dynamo, Teamworks athlete management systems and Performance dashboards and visualization tools 

Requirements


Minimum Qualifications

  • Master's degree (or completion by August 2026) in Exercise Science, Sports Science, Biomechanics, Kinesiology, Performance Analytics, Data Science or Related discipline
  • General knowledge of soccer
  • Capable of working in fast-paced and demanding environments
  • Must be able to connect “micro” details to the “macro” vision and mission
  • Proficient experience with Microsoft Suite (Word, PowerPoint, Excel, and Outlook 

Desired Qualifications

  • Experience with Python, R, Power BI, Tableau, or similar analytics platforms is highly desirable.
  • Experience working with elite or collegiate athletes 
  • Knowledge of athlete monitoring and performance testing 
  • Statistical analysis and data visualization experience 
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills 
  • Ability to work collaboratively within interdisciplinary teams 
  • Curiosity, humility, and a growth mindset 

  

U.S. Soccer offers a comprehensive compensation package, casual work environment, an inclusive culture, and an atmosphere for professional development.


U.S. Soccer is an equal opportunity employer that is committed to diversity, equity, and inclusion, and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any kind on the basis of race, color, sex, religion, national origin, citizenship, pregnancy, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, disability, genetic information, military status, political belief, or any other characteristic protected under the law. This policy applies to all our employment practices within our organization. We strongly encourage women, people of color, LGBTQIA, veterans, parents, and persons with disabilities to apply.

Position Description


U.S. Soccer Federation is seeking a motivated and dependable Assistant Grounds Mechanic to support the maintenance and daily operation of all turf maintenance equipment and facility golf carts at the Arthur M. Blank U.S. Soccer National Training Center, a premier training facility located outside of Atlanta. This position works closely with the Grounds Mechanic and Director of Turf and Grounds to ensure all equipment is maintained in safe, reliable, and efficient operating condition to support world-class training surfaces.


Primary Responsibilities


Equipment Maintenance Support

  • Assist the Head Grounds Mechanic with preventive maintenance and daily servicing of all turf maintenance equipment, including mowers, tractors, utility vehicles, sprayers, and small engine equipment. 
  • Perform basic troubleshooting, inspections, lubrication, blade and reel adjustments, oil changes, tire repairs, and routine maintenance tasks. 
  • Assist with diagnosing mechanical and hydraulic issues and completing repairs in a timely manner. 
  • Maintain cleanliness and organization of the equipment shop, maintenance areas, and storage facilities. 
  • Support equipment setup and preparation for daily trainings, tournaments, and special events. 
  • Help maintain accurate maintenance logs, service records, and parts inventory. 
  • Assist with receiving, organizing, and stocking equipment parts and supplies. 
  • Safely operate equipment as needed to support turf and grounds operations. 

Team & Operational Support

  • Work collaboratively with the Head Grounds Mechanic, Director of Turf and Grounds, and grounds staff to prioritize equipment needs and minimize downtime. 
  • Follow all shop safety standards, operational procedures, and equipment handling guidelines. 
  • Support staff with basic equipment operation guidance and safe-use practices when needed. 
  • Respond promptly to equipment-related issues during trainings, events, and daily operations. 
  • Assist with special projects and facility needs as assigned. 

Requirements


Minimum Qualifications

  • Basic mechanical experience with turf, landscape, agricultural, or automotive equipment preferred. 
  • Working knowledge of small engines, hydraulic systems, diesel engines, and power equipment preferred. 
  • Ability to safely use hand tools, power tools, and diagnostic equipment. 
  • Strong work ethic with willingness to learn and develop technical skills. 
  • General knowledge of soccer.
  • Ability to work independently and as part of a team in a fast-paced environment. 
  • Must  be able to connect “micro” details to the “macro” vision and mission.
  • Proficient experience with Microsoft Suite (Word, PowerPoint, Excel, and Outlook).
  • Good communication and organizational skills. 
  • Technical or vocational training in mechanics or equipment maintenance is a plus. 

Physical Demands

  • Ability to lift up to 50 lbs. and perform physically demanding tasks. 
  • Ability to work outdoors in varying weather conditions, including extreme heat, cold, rain, and snow. 
  • Ability to stand, bend, kneel, climb, and work in various physical positions for extended periods. 
  • Flexibility to work evenings, weekends, holidays, and extended hours as required by training and event schedules.

This policy applies to all our employment practices within our organization. We strongly encourage women, people of color, LGBTQIA, veterans, parents, and persons with disabilities to apply.

job.title: Safeguarding Manager, Youth Engagement
job.html_description:
Description


U.S. Soccer Overview


The U.S. Soccer Federation exists in service to soccer. Our aim is to ignite a national passion for the game. Because we believe that soccer is more than a sport; it is a force for good.


We understand the importance and the power of teamwork, on and off the pitch. That is why we work closely with our Federation partners and members, to inspire, support and guide every level of the game: from the grassroots to the National Teams. We want to bring soccer into every home and every community, right across America. Because we believe that soccer can transform lives like no other sport. Soccer can represent the best of U.S.


U.S. Soccer is in a period of significant growth, with ambitious plans for U.S. Soccer in the near and far future. We are, therefore, looking for dynamic servant leaders to join us on this journey: in service to soccer. Applicants must be able to demonstrate visionary leadership, analytical decision-making, professional flexibility, and an empathic management style that builds bold teams and delivers globally significant results.


Position Description


The Safeguarding Manager, Youth Engagement is U.S. Soccer's subject-matter expert on safeguarding for youth participants of the game. For the purposes of this role, "youth participants" means all under-18 participants, including minor players, minor referees, and other young people who take part in soccer activities, programs, and events. The role leads safeguarding prevention and education across the youth game and provides youth participant expertise across the wider safeguarding team.


At its core, this role is about culture and the young people at the heart of the game. Meeting regulatory requirements is essential, but not the finish line. Success is measured by whether young people feel safe, heard, and genuinely valued in soccer, and whether the adults around them build environments where that is the norm. Youth voice and youth agency are not add-ons to this work; they are its purpose.


This is a standards-and-enablement role. Rather than personally delivering every program, the Manager sets the frameworks, builds the tools and learning, and equips U.S. Soccer staff, Member Organizations, and partners to create and sustain safe, healthy environments themselves. Given a period of significant growth and major events, priorities will be delivered in phases, sequenced with the Vice President of Safeguarding: foundational standards and education first, then deeper assurance and member capability over time.


To succeed, the Manager brings deep expertise in safeguarding and child protection, a strong command of the regulatory landscape governing minor athletes within the Olympic and Paralympic Movement, and a proven ability to translate standards into practical policy, education, and culture across grassroots, community, and elite settings. Above all, the Manager is committed to working directly with youth athletes, championing their voice, agency, and wellbeing at every stage of their participation.


The role contributes across U.S. Soccer's safeguarding methodology of prevention, reporting, and response. The Manager designs and embeds the policies, learning, and pathways that prevent harm before it occurs. Working closely with the Reporting and Resolution team, the Manager also helps build clear, trusted reporting systems, ensuring concerns can be raised easily, disclosures are acted on appropriately, and learning flows back into prevention. The Manager supports this function as an expert but does not perform case management; intake, investigation, and adjudication sit with the Reporting and Resolution team and the U.S. Center for SafeSport, in line with federal law and U.S. Soccer policy.


The role reports to the Vice President of Safeguarding - Prevention & Education, and works closely with the National Team Safeguarding Manager, providing minor-participant expertise wherever minors or participants at heightened risk are involved (including the youth and disability National Teams). It also partners with the Director of Safeguarding Operations, the Reporting and Resolution team, and other programming members, such as Recreation and Soccer Forward.


Primary Responsibilities

  

Subject-Matter Expertise & Sector Leadership

  • Serve as Subject-Matter Expert: Act as a key internal expert on youth athletes and youth participant safeguarding spanning regulation, recognized best practice, and the evidence base for U.S. Soccer. Maintain current expertise in applicable requirements (the U.S. Center for SafeSport Minor Athlete Abuse Prevention Policies (MAAPP), the SafeSport Code, USOPC requirements including evolving background-check and training standards, and applicable state mandatory-reporting law) alongside leading safeguarding frameworks and research, including evidence-based, trauma-informed, and child-centered prevention practice. With the wider Safeguarding team, support the translation of regulatory change and emerging evidence into clear, actionable internal guidance, and contribute to external guidance for Members and partners.
  • Serve as an Advisor: Provide expert advice and support to the wider Safeguarding Team and U.S. Soccer operations wherever youth or participants at heightened risk are involved, including the youth national teams, the disability National Teams, age-group camps, talent-identification events, and the transition of minor participants into the senior environment.
  • Contribute Thought Leadership: Stay at the leading edge of youth safeguarding in soccer, building relationships with U.S. Soccer Members, peer NGBs, and child-protection experts, and researching and briefing the organization on emerging best practices and risks to minor participants. Maintain particular focus on the digital environment, including online grooming, harmful contact through social and gaming platforms, sextortion, image-based abuse, and AI-enabled threats, translating insight into refreshed prevention controls and helping to champion a positive, child-centered safeguarding culture.

Policies, Standards & Safe Environments

  • Develop Policies and Standards: Support the development and maintenance of safeguarding policies, codes of conduct, and operating standards that apply to youth participants, including recreation, community, commercial, and event settings, with practical implementation tools that make them usable for youth, staff, volunteers, contractors, and partners.
  • Advance Inclusive and Accessible Safeguarding: Ensure safeguarding standards, learning, and reporting routes are inclusive and accessible through addressing the elevated and specific risks faced by disabled participants and other groups at heightened risk across the youth and grassroots game, including disability soccer programs, and equipping programs to make safe participation genuinely accessible to all.
  • Enable Safe Engagement in Youth Activities: Set and advise on safeguarding standards for any activity that involves or depicts youth participants, including photo and video shoots, public appearances, ambassador and talent engagements, and the use of minors' image and likeness in marketing, merchandise, and collectibles. Define consent, chaperoning, and supervision requirements in partnership with Marketing, Commercial, and Legal, keeping young people's dignity and agency at the center of how they are represented.
  • Enable Safe Facilities, Events, and Activations: Provide the safeguarding standards, planning, and risk-assessment support that keep minors safe at U.S. Soccer venues, events, and activations whenever they are present or their interests are engaged, including the national training center, visiting youth groups, camps, clinics, tours, and event-day supervision, trusted-adult, and reporting arrangements. Support U.S. Soccer Members in building the same safe practices for their own youth participants.

Education, Training & Capacity Building

  • Build Learning and Education Assets: Lead the development of safeguarding learning content with and for youth participants and the adults who engage with them, using blended digital, virtual, and in-person delivery designed to be age-appropriate, accessible, and effective across a diverse, multilingual community.
  • Build Member Capacity: Strengthen the safeguarding capacity and capability of Member Organizations through toolkits, train-the-trainer models, and ongoing support, scaling consistent standards across a membership of millions. This includes supporting the Safe Soccer Clearance program from a youth participant perspective, so that the training, screening, and clearance of those working with minors remain appropriate and effective.

Program Safeguarding: Recreation & Community

  • Support Recreation and Schools Programming: Act as a safeguarding partner to Soccer in Schools and recreation initiatives, ensuring program models, screening, supervision standards, and reporting pathways are appropriate for school and community delivery.
  • Embed Safeguarding in Community Engagement: Build safeguarding into Soccer Forward and community and social-impact programming through a child-centered, inclusive, “safeguarding-by-design” approach.

Collaboration, Monitoring & Continuous Improvement

  • Make Reporting and Response Accessible to Minors and Communities: Work with the Reporting and Resolution team to ensure reporting and response systems are appropriate, accessible, and trusted for youth participants and the communities they come from. Routes for raising concerns should be age-appropriate, low-barrier, culturally and linguistically accessible, and well understood by young people, families, and grassroots organizations, with disclosures recognized and escalated appropriately. 
  • Collaborate Across the Organization: Partner across the Reporting and Resolution team, Legal, Coaching Education, Commercial, Facilities, and Membership to align policy, education, and delivery, and feed learning back into prevention.

Requirements


Minimum Qualifications

  • Education: Bachelor’s degree in Child Protection, Social Work, Education, Public Health, Sport Management, Criminal Justice, or a related field (or equivalent experience)
  • Safeguarding Expertise & Experience: Minimum of 5 years in safeguarding, child protection, or minor welfare, including hands-on experience designing and implementing prevention measures and delivering policy and education programs at scale, experience with safeguarding in a sporting environment and a strong working knowledge of the U.S. child-protection landscape (U.S. Center for SafeSport and MAAPP requirements; state mandatory-reporting obligations), with a demonstrated track record of building child-centered, youth-voice-led safeguarding culture, not only implementing policy and meeting compliance requirements
  • Learning Design: Demonstrated experience designing and delivering effective learning and training frameworks (digital, blended, and in-person) for varied audiences including young people, and leveraging digital learning ecosystems (LMS, content delivery, learning analytics), with awareness of online-safety and digital-risk trends affecting young people
  • Leadership & Project Management: Proven ability to lead projects, influence across functions without direct authority, and contribute to strategic decision-making; capable of working in fast-paced and demanding environments
  • Judgment & Discretion: Excellent judgment, the ability to recognize risk and the limits of the role and escalate appropriately, and the highest standards of integrity and confidentiality when handling sensitive matters
  • Other Requirements: Ability to pass a background check and complete SafeSport / safeguarding training; willingness to travel and to work occasional evenings and weekends around camps and events
  • Language: English required
  • General knowledge of soccer
  • Capable of working in fast-paced and demanding environments
  • Must be able to connect “micro” details to the “macro” vision and mission
  • Proficient experience with Microsoft Suite (Word, PowerPoint, Excel, and Outlook)


Desired Qualifications

  • Experience within an NGB, the Olympic & Paralympic Movement, sport, or education, and with inclusive, accessible safeguarding for disabled participants and adults at risk
  • Spanish proficiency

job.plain_text_description:
Description
U.S. Soccer Overview
The U.S. Soccer Federation exists in service to soccer. Our aim is to ignite a national passion for the game. Because we believe that soccer is more than a sport; it is a force for good.
We understand the importance and the power of teamwork, on and off the pitch. That is why we work closely with our Federation partners and members, to inspire, support and guide every level of the game: from the grassroots to the National Teams. We want to bring soccer into every home and every community, right across America. Because we believe that soccer can transform lives like no other sport. Soccer can represent the best of U.S.
U.S. Soccer is in a period of significant growth, with ambitious plans for U.S. Soccer in the near and far future. We are, therefore, looking for dynamic servant leaders to join us on this journey: in service to soccer. Applicants must be able to demonstrate visionary leadership, analytical decision-making, professional flexibility, and an empathic management style that builds bold teams and delivers globally significant results.
Position Description
The Safeguarding Manager, Youth Engagement is U.S. Soccer's subject-matter expert on safeguarding for youth participants of the game. For the purposes of this role, "youth participants" means all under-18 participants, including minor players, minor referees, and other young people who take part in soccer activities, programs, and events. The role leads safeguarding prevention and education across the youth game and provides youth participant expertise across the wider safeguarding team.
At its core, this role is about culture and the young people at the heart of the game. Meeting regulatory requirements is essential, but not the finish line. Success is measured by whether young people feel safe, heard, and genuinely valued in soccer, and whether the adults around them build environments where that is the norm. Youth voice and youth agency are not add-ons to this work; they are its purpose.
This is a standards-and-enablement role. Rather than personally delivering every program, the Manager sets the frameworks, builds the tools and learning, and equips U.S. Soccer staff, Member Organizations, and partners to create and sustain safe, healthy environments themselves. Given a period of significant growth and major events, priorities will be delivered in phases, sequenced with the Vice President of Safeguarding: foundational standards and education first, then deeper assurance and member capability over time.
To succeed, the Manager brings deep expertise in safeguarding and child protection, a strong command of the regulatory landscape governing minor athletes within the Olympic and Paralympic Movement, and a proven ability to translate standards into practical policy, education, and culture across grassroots, community, and elite settings. Above all, the Manager is committed to working directly with youth athletes, championing their voice, agency, and wellbeing at every stage of their participation.
The role contributes across U.S. Soccer's safeguarding methodology of prevention, reporting, and response. The Manager designs and embeds the policies, learning, and pathways that prevent harm before it occurs. Working closely with the Reporting and Resolution team, the Manager also helps build clear, trusted reporting systems, ensuring concerns can be raised easily, disclosures are acted on appropriately, and learning flows back into prevention. The Manager supports this function as an expert but does not perform case management; intake, investigation, and adjudication sit with the Reporting and Resolution team and the U.S. Center for SafeSport, in line with federal law and U.S. Soccer policy.
The role reports to the Vice President of Safeguarding - Prevention & Education, and works closely with the National Team Safeguarding Manager, providing minor-participant expertise wherever minors or participants at heightened risk are involved (including the youth and disability National Teams). It also partners with the Director of Safeguarding Operations, the Reporting and Resolution team, and other programming members, such as Recreation and Soccer Forward.
Primary Responsibilities
Subject-Matter Expertise & Sector Leadership
- Serve as Subject-Matter Expert: Act as a key internal expert on youth athletes and youth participant safeguarding spanning regulation, recognized best practice, and the evidence base for U.S. Soccer. Maintain current expertise in applicable requirements (the U.S. Center for SafeSport Minor Athlete Abuse Prevention Policies (MAAPP), the SafeSport Code, USOPC requirements including evolving background-check and training standards, and applicable state mandatory-reporting law) alongside leading safeguarding frameworks and research, including evidence-based, trauma-informed, and child-centered prevention practice. With the wider Safeguarding team, support the translation of regulatory change and emerging evidence into clear, actionable internal guidance, and contribute to external guidance for Members and partners. - Serve as an Advisor: Provide expert advice and support to the wider Safeguarding Team and U.S. Soccer operations wherever youth or participants at heightened risk are involved, including the youth national teams, the disability National Teams, age-group camps, talent-identification events, and the transition of minor participants into the senior environment. - Contribute Thought Leadership: Stay at the leading edge of youth safeguarding in soccer, building relationships with U.S. Soccer Members, peer NGBs, and child-protection experts, and researching and briefing the organization on emerging best practices and risks to minor participants. Maintain particular focus on the digital environment, including online grooming, harmful contact through social and gaming platforms, sextortion, image-based abuse, and AI-enabled threats, translating insight into refreshed prevention controls and helping to champion a positive, child-centered safeguarding culture.
Policies, Standards & Safe Environments
- Develop Policies and Standards:Support the development and maintenance of safeguarding policies, codes of conduct, and operating standards that apply to youth participants, including recreation, community, commercial, and event settings, with practical implementation tools that make them usable for youth, staff, volunteers, contractors, and partners. - Advance Inclusive and Accessible Safeguarding: Ensure safeguarding standards, learning, and reporting routes are inclusive and accessible through addressing the elevated and specific risks faced by disabled participants and other groups at heightened risk across the youth and grassroots game, including disability soccer programs, and equipping programs to make safe participation genuinely accessible to all. - Enable Safe Engagement in Youth Activities: Set and advise on safeguarding standards for any activity that involves or depicts youth participants, including photo and video shoots, public appearances, ambassador and talent engagements, and the use of minors' image and likeness in marketing, merchandise, and collectibles. Define consent, chaperoning, and supervision requirements in partnership with Marketing, Commercial, and Legal, keeping young people's dignity and agency at the center of how they are represented. - Enable Safe Facilities, Events, and Activations: Provide the safeguarding standards, planning, and risk-assessment support that keep minors safe at U.S. Soccer venues, events, and activations whenever they are present or their interests are engaged, including the national training center, visiting youth groups, camps, clinics, tours, and event-day supervision, trusted-adult, and reporting arrangements. Support U.S. Soccer Members in building the same safe practices for their own youth participants.
Education, Training & Capacity Building
- Build Learning and Education Assets:Lead the development of safeguarding learning content with and for youth participants and the adults who engage with them, using blended digital, virtual, and in-person delivery designed to be age-appropriate, accessible, and effective across a diverse, multilingual community. - Build Member Capacity: Strengthen the safeguarding capacity and capability of Member Organizations through toolkits, train-the-trainer models, and ongoing support, scaling consistent standards across a membership of millions. This includes supporting the Safe Soccer Clearance program from a youth participant perspective, so that the training, screening, and clearance of those working with minors remain appropriate and effective.
Program Safeguarding: Recreation & Community
- Support Recreation and Schools Programming:Act as a safeguarding partner to Soccer in Schools and recreation initiatives, ensuring program models, screening, supervision standards, and reporting pathways are appropriate for school and community delivery. - Embed Safeguarding in Community Engagement: Build safeguarding into Soccer Forward and community and social-impact programming through a child-centered, inclusive, “safeguarding-by-design” approach.
Collaboration, Monitoring & Continuous Improvement
- Make Reporting and Response Accessible to Minors and Communities:Work with the Reporting and Resolution team to ensure reporting and response systems are appropriate, accessible, and trusted for youth participants and the communities they come from. Routes for raising concerns should be age-appropriate, low-barrier, culturally and linguistically accessible, and well understood by young people, families, and grassroots organizations, with disclosures recognized and escalated appropriately. - Collaborate Across the Organization:Partner across the Reporting and Resolution team, Legal, Coaching Education, Commercial, Facilities, and Membership to align policy, education, and delivery, and feed learning back into prevention.
Requirements
Minimum Qualifications
- Education: Bachelor’s degree in Child Protection, Social Work, Education, Public Health, Sport Management, Criminal Justice, or a related field (or equivalent experience) - Safeguarding Expertise & Experience:Minimum of 5 years in safeguarding, child protection, or minor welfare, including hands-on experience designing and implementing prevention measures and delivering policy and education programs at scale, experience with safeguarding in a sporting environment and a strong working knowledge of the U.S. child-protection landscape (U.S. Center for SafeSport and MAAPP requirements; state mandatory-reporting obligations), with a demonstrated track record of building child-centered, youth-voice-led safeguarding culture, not only implementing policy and meeting compliance requirements - Learning Design:Demonstrated experience designing and delivering effective learning and training frameworks (digital, blended, and in-person) for varied audiences including young people, and leveraging digital learning ecosystems (LMS, content delivery, learning analytics), with awareness of online-safety and digital-risk trends affecting young people - Leadership & Project Management:Proven ability to lead projects, influence across functions without direct authority, and contribute to strategic decision-making; capable of working in fast-paced and demanding environments - Judgment & Discretion: Excellent judgment, the ability to recognize risk and the limits of the role and escalate appropriately, and the highest standards of integrity and confidentiality when handling sensitive matters - Other Requirements:Ability to pass a background check and complete SafeSport / safeguarding training; willingness to travel and to work occasional evenings and weekends around camps and events - Language: English required - General knowledge of soccer - Capable of working in fast-paced and demanding environments - Must be able to connect “micro” details to the “macro” vision and mission - Proficient experience with Microsoft Suite (Word, PowerPoint, Excel, and Outlook)
Desired Qualifications
- Experience within an NGB, the Olympic & Paralympic Movement, sport, or education, and with inclusive, accessible safeguarding for disabled participants and adults at risk - Spanish proficiency

job.title: Senior Software Engineer
job.html_description:
Description


U.S. Soccer Overview


The U.S. Soccer Federation exists in service to soccer. Our aim is to ignite a national passion for the game. Because we believe that soccer is more than a sport; it is a force for good.


We understand the importance and the power of teamwork, on and off the pitch. That is why we work closely with our Federation partners and members, to inspire, support and guide every level of the game: from the grassroots to the National Teams. We want to bring soccer into every home and every community, right across America. Because we believe that soccer can transform lives like no other sport. Soccer can represent the best of U.S.


U.S. Soccer is in a period of significant growth, with ambitious plans for U.S. Soccer in the near and far future. We are, therefore, looking for dynamic servant leaders to join us on this journey: in service to soccer. Applicants must be able to demonstrate visionary leadership, analytical decision-making, professional flexibility, and an empathic management style that builds bold teams and delivers globally significant results.


Position Description


The Senior Software Engineer will provide hands-on technical leadership for the shared platform capabilities that powers U.S. Soccer's Soccer Services and Learning Center experiences. This engineer will lead the design and delivery of reusable components, services, content models, and workflow patterns that can be composed across public, authenticated, learner, and administrator experiences serving coaches, referees, educators, Organization Members, players, parents, and other participants across the 

country.


Based at U.S. Soccer’s National Training Center, this role will be a visible Product & Technology partner for Soccer Services and Learning Center stakeholders. The Senior Software Engineer will participate in planning and working sessions, translate operational and product needs into clear technical direction, communicate tradeoffs and delivery risk, and build trusted relationships across engineering, product, design, content and curriculum, data, and soccer operations.


The work spans education, course management, licensing and certification, member and organization services, registration and application workflows, safeguarding and compliance, content delivery, and administrative operations. This engineer will establish and extend proven patterns across clear boundaries between experience, content, identity, and operational systems; guide incremental modernization while protecting current service; and make U.S. Soccer’s design, accessibility, security, reliability, and performance standards the default.


This is a senior individual-contributor role for a systems-oriented full-stack engineer who combines architecture judgment with a willingness to work directly in the code. Depending on the product area, the engineer may work with technologies such as Go, PHP/Laravel, JavaScript and TypeScript, Sanity, PostgreSQL, Auth0/OIDC, AWS, containers and Kubernetes, messaging platforms, and CDN/edge delivery.


Primary Responsibilities

  • Lead the technical design and end-to-end delivery of production capabilities across Soccer.
  • Services and the Learning Center—from discovery and architecture through implementation, testing, release, monitoring, and iteration.
  • Serve as an in-person Product & Technology partner at the National Training Center; participate in stakeholder meetings, clarify complex requirements, surface dependencies and risks, and translate product and operational goals into practical delivery plans.
  • Establish and evolve reusable platform building blocks—including user-interface components, service contracts, content models, templates, and workflow patterns—that solve shared problems and can be adopted consistently across products.
  • Deliver learner-, member-, and administrator-facing experiences such as dashboards, course modules, video review, assessment and certification flows, renewals, progress tracking, in person clinic logistics, registration, eligibility, document review, approvals, and administrative tools.
  • Provide technical leadership through architecture and code reviews, design facilitation, documentation, mentorship, and constructive feedback; help engineers make sound decisions and raise the quality and consistency of the team’s work.
  • Design and operate backend services, APIs, data models, event-driven workflows, and integrations across identity, content, learning, member, analytics, and third-party systems, with clear contracts and strong auditability.
  • Lead incremental modernization of existing workflows and integrations while maintaining compatibility, data integrity, and reliable service for current users.
  • Set and uphold standards for automated testing, continuous delivery, observability, performance, scalability, resilience, accessibility, privacy, role-based access, and security; lead diagnosis and durable resolution of production incidents.
  • Partner with engineering and product leadership on roadmaps, technical strategy, sequencing, estimation, staffing dependencies, and measurable outcomes while communicating decisions clearly to technical and nontechnical audiences.

Requirements


Minimum Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in software engineering or related field. 
  • 7+ years of professional software-engineering experience building and operating production applications, including at least 3 years' operating at a senior or technical-lead level.
  • Demonstrated success leading the design and delivery of complex full-stack systems across frontend, backend, APIs, data, integrations, and cloud infrastructure.
  • Strong HTML, CSS, and modern JavaScript or TypeScript skills, plus deep experience with at least one server-side language and relational data modeling.
  • Experience designing maintainable service boundaries, web APIs, distributed or event-driven workflows, and integrations with identity or other enterprise platforms.
  • Strong understanding of software architecture, automated testing, version control, code review, continuous integration and delivery, observability, and safe production operations.
  • Experience building secure, privacy-aware, responsive, and accessible digital experiences and protecting data integrity during migrations and integrations.
  • Demonstrated ability to diagnose issues across application code, infrastructure, logs, metrics, and user-reported behavior; able to lead incident response and carry fixes safely into production.
  • Track record of improving engineering practices and mentoring other engineers through clear technical direction, collaborative reviews, and constructive feedback.
  • Excellent written, verbal, and interpersonal communication skills, including the ability to build trust with nontechnical partners, facilitate decisions, and explain tradeoffs in an in-person, cross-functional environment.
  • Ability to work effectively from the National Training Center in a fast-moving environment, manage competing priorities, and connect implementation details to broader product and organizational goals.
  • General knowledge of soccer and its ecosystem, or a demonstrated interest in learning it quickly.
  • Must be able to connect “micro” details to the “macro” vision and mission.
  • Proficient experience with Microsoft Suite (Word, PowerPoint, Excel, and Outlook).

Desired Qualifications

  • Experience with technologies relevant to the current environment, such as Go, PHP/Laravel, JavaScript/TypeScript, Sanity or another headless CMS, PostgreSQL, Auth0/OIDC, or similar tools.
  • Experience designing systems with CQRS and event sourcing, and building APIs that use JSON Patch or comparable standards for partial resource updates.
  • Experience with distributed systems, asynchronous processing, and messaging or streaming platforms such as Kafka or RabbitMQ.
  • Experience deploying and operating cloud applications using AWS, containers, Kubernetes, CDN/edge services, and modern observability practices.
  • Experience building learning-management, education, certification, membership, eligibility, compliance, document-review, or other multi-role workflow products.
  • Experience with design systems, WCAG 2.1 AA, media-rich experiences, and products designed for low-bandwidth or older-device contexts.
  • Experience integrating identity, content, CRM, analytics, or third-party platforms while maintaining data quality, security, and auditability.
  • Background in or passion for soccer, sports, education, or membership-based organizations
  • Spanish-language proficiency is a plus.


U.S. Soccer offers a comprehensive compensation package, casual work environment, an inclusive culture, and an atmosphere for professional development.


U.S. Soccer is an equal opportunity employer that is committed to diversity, equity, and inclusion, and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any kind on the basis of race, color, sex, religion, national origin, citizenship, pregnancy, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, disability, genetic information, military status, political belief, or any other characteristic protected under the law. This policy applies to all our employment practices within our organization. We strongly encourage women, people of color, LGBTQIA, veterans, parents, and persons with disabilities to apply.

job.html_description:
Description


U.S. Soccer Overview


The U.S. Soccer Federation exists in service to soccer. Our aim is to ignite a national passion for the game. Because we believe that soccer is more than a sport; it is a force for good.


We understand the importance and the power of teamwork, on and off the pitch.
