We want to bring soccer into every home and every community, right across America. Because we believe that soccer can transform lives like no other sport. Soccer can represent the best of U.S.


U.S. Soccer is in a period of significant growth, with ambitions plans for U.S. Soccer in the near and far future. We are, therefore, looking for dynamic servant leaders to join us on this journey: in service to soccer. Applicants must be able to demonstrate visionary leadership, analytical decision-making, professional flexibility, and an empathic management style that builds bold teams and delivers globally significant results.

  

We are thrilled to launch our third annual Summer Internship Program, specifically for college students who live in the metro Atlanta, Georgia area either during the school year or over the summer.

Position Description


We are seeking motivated and enthusiastic interns to join our team for a 12-week internship program. As an intern, you will have the opportunity to gain hands-on experience in your chosen department, work on meaningful projects, and develop valuable professional skills. You will collaborate with experienced professionals, attend training sessions, and participate in networking events designed to enhance your career development.

Requirements


General Qualifications and Requirements

  • Minimum GPA: 3.0
  • Enrolled in a 4-year undergraduate program with anticipated graduation year of 2028 or 2029
  • Able to participate in this 12-week internship during the summer
  • Able to dedicate 40 hours per week to this internship
  • Able to work in-person at U.S. Soccer’s Fayetteville, GA office at least 3 days per week
  • Strong attention to detail and analytical / problem-solving skills 
  • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills 
  • Ability to prioritize tasks and work effectively in a fast-paced environment
  • Recommended: Participation and interest in soccer/athletics; campus involvement and leadership
  • Deep ties to the Atlanta area – either currently living in metro Atlanta or from the area with a desire to build a career here post-graduation

Perks and Benefits

  • Professional growth & networking: weekly professional development sessions with leaders from across the organization and U.S. soccer ecosystem, meaningful, resume-building work in one of 15+ departments, with personalized mentorship and support, regular networking and social events with fellow interns and full-time staff, official U.S. Soccer gear and intern headshots provided
  • Behind-the-scenes access: experience the lead-up to the 2027 FIFA World Cup from inside the U.S. Soccer Federation, attend a U.S. National Team training camp and an Atlanta United match as part of the program, daily access to the Arthur M. Blank National Training Center
  • Financial support: Salary: $20/hour, Transportation costs will be covered by U.S. Soccer for the duration of the internship (either mileage reimbursement or Uber/Lyft pass)

  

*IMPORTANT: Application instructions*
As part of the application, you will be asked to respond to three (3) short essay questions. Please note that our system does not allow you to save progress, so you’ll need to complete and submit your application in one sitting.


We're excited to hear your authentic voice and perspective. Please submit original essay responses written in your own words. Responses that rely substantially on AI-generated content will not be considered.


A cover letter is not required. If you have any questions, please reach out to internships@ussoccer.org. 

 
Application process and next steps

Thank you for your interest in the U.S. Soccer Internship Program. Applications will be reviewed this fall, and interview invitations will be shared via email.

We are thrilled to launch our third annual Summer Internship Program, specifically for college students who live in the metro Atlanta, Georgia area either during the school year or over the summer.
Position Description
We are seeking motivated and enthusiastic interns to join our team for a 12-week internship program. As an intern, you will have the opportunity to gain hands-on experience in your chosen department, work on meaningful projects, and develop valuable professional skills. You will collaborate with experienced professionals, attend training sessions, and participate in networking events designed to enhance your career development.
Requirements
General Qualifications and Requirements
- Minimum GPA: 3.0 - Enrolled in a 4-year undergraduate program with anticipated graduation year of 2028 or 2029 - Able to participate in this 12-week internship during the summer - Able to dedicate 40 hours per week to this internship - Able to work in-person at U.S. Soccer’s Fayetteville, GA office at least 3 days per week - Strong attention to detail and analytical / problem-solving skills - Excellent communication and interpersonal skills - Ability to prioritize tasks and work effectively in a fast-paced environment - Recommended: Participation and interest in soccer/athletics; campus involvement and leadership - Deep ties to the Atlanta area – either currently living in metro Atlanta or from the area with a desire to build a career here post-graduation
Perks and Benefits
- Professional growth & networking: weekly professional development sessions with leaders from across the organization and U.S. soccer ecosystem, meaningful, resume-building work in one of 15+ departments, with personalized mentorship and support, regular networking and social events with fellow interns and full-time staff, official U.S. Soccer gear and intern headshots provided - Behind-the-scenes access: experience the lead-up to the 2027 FIFA World Cup from inside the U.S. Soccer Federation, attend a U.S. National Team training camp and an Atlanta United match as part of the program, daily access to the Arthur M. Blank National Training Center - Financial support: Salary: $20/hour, Transportation costs will be covered by U.S. Soccer for the duration of the internship (either mileage reimbursement or Uber/Lyft pass)

job.title: Senior Coordinator, Media Operations
job.html_description:
Description


U.S. Soccer Overview


The U.S. Soccer Federation exists in service to soccer. Our aim is to ignite a national passion for the game. Because we believe that soccer is more than a sport; it is a force for good.


We understand the importance and the power of teamwork, on and off the pitch. That is why we work closely with our Federation partners and members, to inspire, support and guide every level of the game: from the grassroots to the National Teams. We want to bring soccer into every home and every community, right across America. Because we believe that soccer can transform lives like no other sport. Soccer can represent the best of U.S.


U.S. Soccer is in a period of significant growth, with ambitious plans for U.S. Soccer in the near and far future. We are, therefore, looking for dynamic servant leaders to join us on this journey: in service to soccer. Applicants must be able to demonstrate visionary leadership, analytical decision-making, professional flexibility, and an empathic management style that builds bold teams and delivers globally significant results.


Position Description


U.S. Soccer is seeking a Sr. Coordinator, Media Operations to help deliver best-in-class media operations across the Federation’s 27 National Teams and major events, with a primary focus on the U.S. Men’s and Women’s National Teams.


Reporting to the Vice President, Communications, this role will be responsible for planning and executing media operations for National Team matches, camps, tournaments and other Federation events. The Sr. Coordinator will serve as a key operational contact for media and work closely with National Team press officers, Sporting, Event Operations, Broadcast, Security, Commercial and venue partners to ensure media needs are thoughtfully planned and seamlessly executed.


The ideal candidate is highly organized, detail-oriented and comfortable working in fast-paced, high-profile environments. This individual should understand the needs of working media, anticipate operational challenges and be able to independently manage multiple priorities and stakeholders while delivering a consistent, professional media experience.


The Sr. Coordinator will work cross-functionally with Communications, Sporting, Event Operations, Media, Security, Ticketing and venue partners to ensure media requirements are integrated into event planning and that U.S. Soccer delivers a consistent, professional media experience across its National Teams and events.


Primary Responsibilities

  • Plan, coordinate and execute media operations for U.S. Soccer National Team matches, camps, tournaments and Federation events, with primary focus on the Men’s and Women’s National Teams and support across all 27 National Teams as needed.
  • Manage media accreditation from application through event-day execution, including reviewing requests, assigning appropriate access, credential production and distribution, and troubleshooting accreditation issues.
  • Serve as a primary onsite point of contact for credentialed media, providing timely information, responding to questions and resolving operational issues.
  • Coordinate media facilities and operational requirements, including press boxes, media workrooms, press conference areas, mixed zones, photographer work areas and field-level positions, media entrances, connectivity, catering and other event-specific needs; manage photographer access and credential/bib distribution as required.
  • Manage media access and movement throughout venues, ensuring credentialed media are appropriately positioned, and event-specific access policies are followed.
  • Partner with venues and internal stakeholders in advance of matches and events to assess media infrastructure, determine operational needs and develop event-specific media operations plans; conduct pre-event walkthroughs and readiness checks to ensure media facilities, signage, technology and services meet established standards.
  • Partner closely with National and Youth Teams press officer to support player and coach media availability, live and virtual press conferences, training access and other team communications needs.
  • Develop and distribute media advisories and operational communications with accreditation details, schedules, access information, parking, media availability and other event logistics. Schedule virtual press conferences, provide links and meeting invites to all pertinent parties, and assist in execution.
  • Ensure U.S. Soccer Media Guidelines and event-specific access policies are consistently implemented, creating a professional working environment for journalists while protecting team needs and the rights of U.S. Soccer’s media partners.
  • Research local media markets and maintain accurate media lists and databases to support National Team and Federation communications efforts.
  • Build and maintain relationships with media operations contacts at venues, FIFA Member Associations, confederations and other soccer organizations.
  • Recruit, brief, train and manage event-day media volunteers, develop staffing plans and assignments, and establish clear roles, expectations and escalation procedures for each event.
  • Manage media operations equipment and inventory to ensure appropriate resources are available for National Team matches and events.
  • Manage media operations vendors, including sourcing services, negotiating agreements, tracking expenses and processing invoices within established budgets.
  • Collaborate with Event Operations, Broadcast, Security, Ticketing, Commercial and other internal teams to ensure media requirements are incorporated into overall event planning.
  • Help develop and implement consistent media operations standards, processes and best practices across U.S. Soccer’s National Teams.
  • Support media operations planning and execution for major international tournaments and other high-profile events hosted or supported by U.S. Soccer.
  • Anticipate operational challenges and independently troubleshoot issues in real time during matches and events.

Requirements


Minimum Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree or equivalent combination of education and relevant professional experience.
  • 3 to 5 years of relevant experience in media operations, communications, public relations, sports communications, event operations or a related field.
  • Demonstrated experience supporting media operations at major live sporting events; experience in professional or international soccer strongly preferred.
  • Strong understanding of media operations, accreditation and credentialing processes, venue access and the needs of working journalists, photographers and broadcasters.
  • Demonstrated ability to independently manage event logistics and multiple stakeholders in fast-paced, high-pressure environments.
  • Strong project management skills, including experience managing timelines, staffing plans, vendors and multiple concurrent workstreams.
  • Strong judgment and demonstrated ability to anticipate issues, solve problems and make decisions in live-event environments.
  • Strong service orientation and demonstrated ability to anticipate and respond to the needs of media and other event stakeholders.
  • Exceptional organizational and time-management skills, with strong attention to detail and the ability to manage multiple events, deadlines and priorities simultaneously.
  • Excellent interpersonal, verbal and written communication skills and demonstrated ability to work effectively with media, athletes, coaches, executives, venue personnel and other high-profile stakeholders.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office; experience with media accreditation, credentialing or event management platforms strongly preferred.
  • Spanish-language proficiency strongly preferred.
  • Ability and willingness to travel up to 50% of the time and work nontraditional hours, including evenings, weekends and holidays, as needed.
  • General knowledge of soccer.
  • Capable of working in fast-paced and demanding environments.
  • Must be able to connect “micro” details to the “macro” vision and mission.


U.S. Soccer offers a comprehensive compensation package, casual work environment, an inclusive culture, and an atmosphere for professional development.


U.S. Soccer is an equal opportunity employer that is committed to diversity, equity, and inclusion, and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any kind on the basis of race, color, sex, religion, national origin, citizenship, pregnancy, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, disability, genetic information, military status, political belief, or any other characteristic protected under the law. This policy applies to all our employment practices within our organization. We strongly encourage women, people of color, LGBTQIA, veterans, parents, and persons with disabilities to apply.

job.title: SVP & Director of Women's and Girls' Soccer
job.html_description:
Description


U.S. Soccer Overview


The U.S. Soccer Federation exists in service to soccer. Our aim is to ignite a national passion for the game. Because we believe that soccer is more than a sport; it is a force for good.


We understand the importance and the power of teamwork, on and off the pitch. That is why we work closely with our Federation partners and members, to inspire, support and guide every level of the game: from the grassroots to the National Teams. We want to bring soccer into every home and every community, right across America. Because we believe that soccer can transform lives like no other sport. Soccer can represent the best of U.S.


U.S. Soccer is in a period of significant growth, with ambitious plans for U.S. Soccer in the near and far future. We are, therefore, looking for dynamic servant leaders to join us on this journey: in service to soccer. Applicants must be able to demonstrate visionary leadership, analytical decision-making, professional flexibility, and an empathic management style that builds bold teams and delivers globally significant results.


Position Description


To achieve our generational ambitions of U.S. Soccer Success and U.S. Soccer Everywhere, the United States must have the best club and national team pathway in the world for girls and women. The SVP, Director of Women's and Girls' Soccer represents a new role that will oversee the implementation of our comprehensive Women and Girls Strategy. This strategy sets both our strategic and technical foundation. It is a senior executive role that will be part of USSF’s Executive Leadership Team and report directly to our Chief Operating Officer. This leader will partner closely with the Head Coach and technical leaders of the U.S. Women's National Team, ensuring that their insight and expertise is built into the pathway and that a female lens is applied to all dimensions of American soccer - from recreational soccer in communities through to our National Team program.


In this role, this person will engage leaders throughout the American female soccer ecosystem – including professional leagues and clubs, college programs, and youth leagues and clubs – to align incentives and create environments that foster elite player development. The scope of this role will require significant leadership agility, from shaping the multi-year pathway strategy and mapping the financial implications, to working on strategies to best deploy capital to support the women’s game, to working with youth organizations on their soccer plans, to conducting player development discussions with pro teams. This mandate demands a sophisticated leader capable of influencing a broad and varied set of stakeholders. They will partner with constituents inside and outside of the federation, including both deeply technical soccer experts and committed business-oriented investors and sponsors, to execute the strategy.


The person should have a deep understanding of the American soccer ecosystem, and the ability to build trusted relationships at all levels. The ideal candidate also would bring an understanding of the global soccer landscape, and where the U.S. could learn from or differentiate from to gain competitive advantages.

The role will be based in Atlanta at U.S. Soccer’s Arthur M. Blank National Training Center.


Primary Responsibilities


In summary, the SVP & Director of Women’s and Girls’ Soccer will: 


Lead:

  • The implementation of U.S. Soccer’s Women & Girls Strategy in collaboration with all relevant stakeholders in the soccer ecosystem
  • The processes to enhance an integrated system that consistently creates world-class players. This includes systems to measure, monitor, and advance talent identification and player development in collaboration with leaders throughout the U.S. amateur and professional leagues (including the Chief Soccer Officers, Owners, Academy Directors, and Team Presidents).
  • The activities to drive greater investment and visibility for the women’s and girls’ game in the ecosystem, including driving greater participation, fan engagement, innovation, and partnerships
  • The public communication of our women’s and girls’ soccer performance and progress throughout the American soccer ecosystem, including through the media and at major events
  • An environment and culture for the people within the broader team to grow and thrive

Oversee and Develop:

  • A team of highly capable, accomplished technical leaders who drive the daily execution of our Women’s and Girls’ Strategy within National Team environments and processes. This team includes our Technical Lead (Women and Girls Head of Development Teams) - who leads WNT and YNT alignment, methodology, player Individual Development Plans (IDP) with clubs/colleges, YNT coach development, and YNT games program - and experts in other technical areas such as Talent Identification, Goalkeeping, and Coaching. The group must work together to position our Youth National Team program for success. The Director of Soccer supports, empowers, and develops these leaders in a collaborative, high-performance team environment.

Partner with:

  • The CEO, COO and other senior executives to advance the Federation’s overall strategy In Service to Soccer
  • The WNT Strategy team to ensure the WNT Strategy is built into the youth pathway and we are preparing as many players for success in the senior team environment as possible
  • The SVP & Director of Men’s and Boys’ Soccer to ensure alignment and coverage between the programs, establishing a shared set of ideas, best practices, and infrastructure while also leaving space for the uniqueness of each environment and pathway

Requirements


Desired Qualifications  

  • Significant executive leadership experience within soccer or sports
  • Experience leading a large multi-functional team, including management of budgets and personnel
  • Experience developing and implementing strategy across complex organizations and stakeholder environments
  • Experience working with external stakeholders (e.g. investors, owners, donors, sponsors, business partners) to align resources in support of strategic plans and initiatives
  • Experience as a lead spokesperson in high-profile settings
  • Experience working with elite female soccer players
  • Experience working within the professional and pre-professional parts of the American soccer landscape
  • Knowledge of the global soccer landscape, including player development and pathways
  • Experience with utilizing technology and data to drive soccer and organizational decisions


U.S. Soccer offers a comprehensive compensation package, casual work environment, an inclusive culture, and an atmosphere for professional development.


U.S. Soccer is an equal opportunity employer that is committed to diversity, equity, and inclusion, and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any kind on the basis of race, color, sex, religion, national origin, citizenship, pregnancy, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, disability, genetic information, military status, political belief, or any other characteristic protected under the law. This policy applies to all our employment practices within our organization. We strongly encourage women, people of color, LGBTQIA, veterans, parents, and persons with disabilities to apply.

  • The activities to drive greater investment and visibility for soccer throughout the country, including greater participation, fan engagement, innovation, and partnerships
  • The public communication of our men’s and boys’ soccer performance and progress throughout the American soccer ecosystem, including through the media and at major events
  • An environment and culture for the people within the broader team to grow and thrive

Oversee and Develop:

  • A team of highly capable, accomplished technical leaders who drive the daily execution of our National Team environment and processes. This team includes our Technical Lead (Men’s and Boys’ Head of Development Teams) - who leads methodology, player Individual Development Plans (IDP) with clubs/colleges, YNT coach development, and YNT games program - and experts in other technical areas such as Talent Identification, Goalkeeping, and Coaching. The group must work together to position our Youth National Team program for success. The Director of Soccer supports, empowers, and develops these leaders in a collaborative, high-performance team environment.

Partner with:

  • The CEO, COO and other senior executives to advance the Federation’s overall strategy In Service to Soccer
  • The strategy team to ensure the men’s and boys’ soccer strategy is built into the youth pathway and we are preparing as many players for success in the senior team environment as possible
  • The SVP & Director of Women’s and Girls’ Soccer to ensure alignment and coverage between the programs, establishing a shared set of ideas, best practices, and infrastructure while also leaving space for the uniqueness of each environment and pathway

Requirements


Desired Qualifications

  • Significant executive leadership experience within soccer or sports
  • Experience leading a large multi-functional team, including management of budgets and personnel
  • Experience developing and implementing strategy across complex organizations and stakeholder environments
  • Experience working with external stakeholders (e.g. investors, owners, donors, sponsors, business partners) to align resources in support of strategic plans and initiatives
  • Experience as a lead spokesperson in high-profile settings
  • Experience working with elite male soccer players
  • Experience working within the professional and pre-professional parts of the American soccer landscape
  • Knowledge of the global soccer landscape, including player development and pathways
  • Experience with utilizing technology and data to drive soccer and organizational decisions


U.S. Soccer offers a comprehensive compensation package, casual work environment, an inclusive culture, and an atmosphere for professional development.

This policy applies to all our employment practices within our organization. We strongly encourage women, people of color, LGBTQIA, veterans, parents, and persons with disabilities to apply.

job.title: Manager, Fan and Soccer Community Experiences
job.html_description:
Description


U.S. Soccer Overview


The U.S. Soccer Federation exists in service to soccer. Our aim is to ignite a national passion for the game. Because we believe that soccer is more than a sport; it is a force for good.


We understand the importance and the power of teamwork, on and off the pitch. That is why we work closely with our Federation partners and members, to inspire, support and guide every level of the game: from the grassroots to the National Teams. We want to bring soccer into every home and every community, right across America. Because we believe that soccer can transform lives like no other sport. Soccer can represent the best of U.S.


U.S. Soccer is in a period of significant growth, with ambitious plans for U.S. Soccer in the near and far future. We are, therefore, looking for dynamic servant leaders to join us on this journey: in service to soccer. Applicants must be able to demonstrate visionary leadership, analytical decision-making, professional flexibility, and an empathic management style that builds bold teams and delivers globally significant results.


Position Description

  

As soccer becomes one of the fastest-growing sports in the United States, the Manager, Fan and Soccer Community Experiences owns how it feels to be a U.S. Soccer fan — whether this is at matches, special events or digitally. At U.S. Soccer, we work across a range of audiences across the whole soccer community including coaches, players and referees, families, members and clubs who we consider all to be fans


This is a strategic role with three connected mandates. First, it sets the creative and operational standard for national team matchday experience. Second, it builds the programming slate for U.S. Soccer’s tentpole and special event moments — including for big tournaments including World Cup, SheBelieves Cup, Gold Cup or at U.S. Soccer international matches and marquee cultural moments that sit alongside them. Third, and cutting across both, it merges the physical and the digital so that any experience is not a one-day footprint but a connected fan journey: discovered on social, deepened on-site, extended through content, and measured end to end.


This role is a builder of repeatable systems as much as a producer of individual events. It defines the experience framework, playbooks, and quality bar that a growing team, a national vendor base, and a multi-city event calendar can execute against consistently — turning passion for the national teams into durable, measurable fandom.


What Success Looks Like


In year one, this role establishes a defined U.S. Soccer fan and soccer community experience strategy and standard applied consistently across every match and tentpole event; delivers a programming calendar that is planned in advance rather than assembled match to match; and demonstrates, with data, that integrated physical-plus-digital experiences outperform standalone ones on reach, relevancy and revenue.


Key Responsibilities


Strategy, Vision & Experience Standards

  • Own and evolve U.S. Soccer’s fan and soccer community experience strategy across matchday, tentpole, and special event moments, with a focus on emotional resonance, lifelong fandom, and brand affinity.
  • Define the multi-year experiential roadmap and the annual programming calendar, aligning it to business goals and audience expectations.
  • Establish the U.S. Soccer fan and community experience standard — the creative principles, quality bar, and brand guardrails that govern every fan-facing footprint — and build the playbooks that make it repeatable at scale.
  • Serve as an internal and external thought leader on fan and soccer community experiences, representing the discipline with senior stakeholders, partners, host committees, and industry forums.

Matchday Experience

  • Lead the strategy, programming, and execution of all national team matchday experiences, including Block Party, Fan HQ, pre-match fan zones, in-stadium moments, gate giveaways, and thematic experience zones, and how to bring in the wider soccer community.
  • Design the full matchday experiences arc — from the night-before fan party and Block Party through arrival, in-bowl experience, and post-match extension — as a single, intentional journey rather than a set of separate experiences.
  • Champion theme nights and culturally led initiatives that reflect organizational values, celebrate the diversity of the American soccer fanbase, and deepen inclusion.
  • Partner with Partnership Marketing to shape and deliver thematic partner experiences, ensuring commercial integrations enhance rather than interrupt the fan experience and meet best-in-class on-site execution standards.
  • Set venue and host-city experience requirements in partnership with Events, Production, Ticketing, and Security, and hold vendors and internal teams to them.

Tentpole & Special Event Programming

  • Build and own the programming slate for U.S. Soccer’s tentpole moments across major tournaments — World Cup, SheBelieves Cup, Gold Cup, and other marquee competitions and milestone events.
  • Program these moments as content and culture, not just logistics: curate talent, music, food, art, community, creator, and legend-led components that give each event a distinct identity and a reason to attend.
  • Develop repeatable event formats and franchises — watch parties, fan fests, community celebrations, supporter takeovers — that can travel across markets and scale year over year.
  • Lead programming for milestone and special events including grassroots and community moments, tied to national team activity and Federation priorities.
  • Build multi-market and multi-year plans for major competitions, coordinating with host committees, venues, civic organizations, and local partners well ahead of event windows.

Integrated Physical + Digital Fan Experience

  • Own the connection between physical and digital experience: ensure every experience is designed from the outset with a content, social, and data capture plan, not amplified after the fact.
  • Partner with Social, Content, Digital Product, and Communications to build always-on and moment-driven programming that reaches fans who cannot attend in person and converts them into attendees over time.
  • Direct the design of on-site digital touchpoints — app-driven experiences, activations built for capture and sharing, second-screen and in-venue content moments, and registration or data-capture mechanics that feed the fan database.
  • Work with Growth, Lifecycle Marketing, Insiders and other Federation teams to define and deliver a personalized fan journey across live, digital, and community platforms, ensuring experiential moments are triggers within the broader lifecycle rather than isolated events.
  • Partner with Ticketing and Growth Marketing to connect experience programming to attendance, membership, and revenue outcomes.

Partnerships, Supporters & Community

  • Cultivate relationships with supporter groups, vendors, civic organizations, and cultural partners to co-create experiences rooted in authenticity and local relevance.
  • Lead cross-departmental coordination with Events, Production, Ticketing, Consumer Products, Community Relations, Media Partnerships, Communications, and Brand to ensure alignment, consistency, and excellence in execution.
  • Manage agency and vendor relationships end to end, including scoping, selection, briefing, and performance management.

Insights, Measurement & Optimization

  • Establish the KPI framework for fan experience — spanning attendance, sentiment, dwell time, digital reach and engagement, data capture, and downstream ticketing and membership impact — and report against it to senior stakeholders.
  • Partner with the Insights team to analyze fan sentiment, survey feedback, and social performance, and translate findings into concrete changes to programming and design.
  • Run a disciplined test-and-learn approach, piloting new formats and retiring those that do not perform.

Team Leadership, Budget & Operational Excellence

  • Manage, coach, and develop the Fan Engagement Coordinator, setting clear priorities and creating room for that role to own workstreams independently.
  • Build and lead extended matchday and event teams, including seasonal staff, agency partners, and cross-functional working groups.
  • Own the fan experience budget end to end — planning, allocation, tracking, and reconciliation — ensuring resources are directed to the highest-impact moments and delivered on time and on budget.
  • Stay at the forefront of industry innovation in fan experience, live entertainment, and experiential technology, bringing forward ideas that keep U.S. Soccer at the leading edge.

Requirements


Minimum Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in Marketing, Sports Management, Business, or a related field.
  • 6–8+ years of progressive experience in fan experience, experiential marketing, live events, or brand experience within sports, entertainment, or consumer-facing industries.
  • Direct people management experience, including coaching and developing junior staff.
  • Proven experience designing and delivering high-impact experiential programs at national scale, including large-scale or multi-market events.
  • Demonstrated fluency across physical and digital experience — able to brief a content and social team as credibly as a production vendor, and to design experiences for both on-site impact and digital reach.
  • Experience programming events as content: curating talent, cultural partners, and creative components, not only managing logistics.
  • Track record of owning and managing significant event budgets.
  • Comfort using data and fan insight to set strategy, prioritize investment, and evaluate performance.
  • Exceptional cross-functional collaboration, communication, and executive presence.
  • Ability to lead multiple complex initiatives simultaneously in a high-performance, fast-paced environment.
  • Must be able to connect “micro” details to the “macro” vision and mission.
  • Proficient experience with Microsoft Suite (Word, PowerPoint, Excel, and Outlook)Flexibility to work non-traditional hours, including evenings, weekends, and holidays. 
  • Ability to travel approximately 40–50% annually, concentrated in match windows and tentpole event periods.


Desired Qualifications

  • Experience in international soccer, major league sports, music or live entertainment, or global event production.
  • Experience delivering fan experience programs for a large-scale event or major tournament.
  • Expertise in data-driven marketing, loyalty strategy, or direct-to-consumer fan experience design.
  • Bilingual or multicultural fluency to engage diverse audiences.


U.S. Soccer offers a comprehensive compensation package, casual work environment, an inclusive culture, and an atmosphere for professional development.


U.S. Soccer is an equal opportunity employer that is committed to diversity, equity, and inclusion, and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any kind on the basis of race, color, sex, religion, national origin, citizenship, pregnancy, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, disability, genetic information, military status, political belief, or any other characteristic protected under the law. This policy applies to all our employment practices within our organization. We strongly encourage women, people of color, LGBTQIA, veterans, parents, and persons with disabilities to apply.

job.title: Senior Performance Coach, Women’s Youth National Teams (WYNT)
job.html_description:
Description


U.S. Soccer Overview


The U.S. Soccer Federation exists in service to soccer. Our aim is to ignite a national passion for the game. Because we believe that soccer is more than a sport; it is a force for good.


We understand the importance and the power of teamwork, on and off the pitch. That is why we work closely with our Federation partners and members, to inspire, support and guide every level of the game: from the grassroots to the National Teams. We want to bring soccer into every home and every community, right across America. Because we believe that soccer can transform lives like no other sport. Soccer can represent the best of U.S.


U.S. Soccer is in a period of significant growth, with ambitious plans for U.S. Soccer in the near and far future. We are, therefore, looking for dynamic servant leaders to join us on this journey: in service to soccer. Applicants must be able to demonstrate visionary leadership, analytical decision-making, professional flexibility, and an empathic management style that builds bold teams and delivers globally significant results.


Position Description

  

U.S. Soccer is seeking a collaborative and growth-oriented Senior Performance Coach to support the Women’s Youth National Teams. As a member of the Integrated Performance Support (IPS) department, this role will contribute to the delivery and continuous evolution of integrated performance practices through a female lens across camps, competitions, and other player development environments. 


Emphasizing that the female lens is at the heart of everything we do, this role aligns with the WNT strategy while integrating an interdisciplinary approach. This position will collaborate closely with Performance Medicine, Performance Nutrition, Performance & Data Analytics, Performance Innovation, and Technical staff to optimize player availability, development, and performance.


The Senior Performance Coach will support the design and implementation of evidence-informed physical preparation strategies, including readiness and load monitoring, physical testing, strength and conditioning, recovery, and performance planning through a female lens. In partnership with coaches and IPS colleagues, this role will help create world-class player experiences that support both team success and long-term player development.


A key focus of this position will be advancing U.S. Soccer’s commitment to becoming world-leading in female health, development, and performance. Working within the Arthur M. Blank National Training Center, the Senior Performance Coach will contribute to the development of integrated systems, innovative practices, and environments that elevate player care across the Women’s Youth National Team pathway.


The ideal candidate is an intellectually curious practitioner and strong teammate who thrives in collaborative, fast-paced environments, embraces innovation, and is passionate about supporting the growth of elite female players.


Primary Responsibilities


Integrated Performance Delivery

  • Support the delivery of integrated performance services across the U19-U20 Women’s National Team environments, including domestic and international camps and competitions.
  • Contribute to the design and implementation of individual and team-based performance strategies that optimize player availability, development, and performance.
  • Collaborate closely with technical staff on training design, competition preparation, recovery, and long-term player development.
  • Collaborate with WNT, U23 and other WYNT technical, performance, and medical staff to align club, college, and country communications, facilitate the exchange of information, and promote continuity of player care, to ensure smooth player transitions between club and country environments.
  • Travel with Youth National Teams to provide on-site performance support.

Female Health & Performance

  • Advance U.S. Soccer’s commitment to becoming world-leading in female health, development, and performance.
  • Support initiatives related to growth and maturation, female health, injury-risk reduction, and long-term player development.
  • Collaborate with performance medicine, performance nutrition, and technical staff to optimize player readiness and availability.

Physical Preparation & Performance Science

  • Support the design and implementation of physical preparation programs (using Teamworks AMS), including strength and conditioning, recovery, and load management strategies.
  • Oversee player monitoring, physical testing, and performance profiling systems to support evidence-informed decision-making.
  • Utilize technologies including PlayerData GPS, VALD performance tools, OURA, FitrWoman, Raw Stadia, and a growing portfolio of technologies to support health and performance.
  • Translate objective performance data into actionable insights for players, coaches, and IPS staff.
  • Contribute to the ongoing development of best practices in performance science across the women’s pathway.

Integrated Performance Support Collaboration

  • Serve as a key member of the Integrated Performance Support (IPS) team, supporting world-class player care and performance services.
  • Collaborate with Performance Medicine, Performance Nutrition, Performance & Data Analytics, Performance Innovation, and technical staff to support integrated decision-making and player development.
  • Execute and continuously improve performance methodologies, testing protocols, and operational standards across camps and competitions.
  • Contribute to a culture of curiosity, collaboration, accountability, and continuous learning.
  • Support the onboarding and development of network practitioners and interns as needed.

Data, Analytics & Innovation

  • Oversee the collection, interpretation, communication, and storage of player performance data in accordance with U.S. Soccer standards.
  • Partner with analytics and innovation teams to develop and implement novel approaches to player monitoring and decision-making.
  • Support longitudinal player profiling and talent development initiatives across the Women’s pathway.
  • Build and maintain relationships with clubs, universities, and external partners to facilitate the exchange of performance information and best practices.
  • Contribute to the National Training Center as a world-class environment for integrated athlete support, innovation, and organizational learning.

Requirements


Minimum Qualifications

  • Master’s degree or higher in Sport Science, Exercise Physiology, Kinesiology, Strength & Conditioning, or related field.
  • Demonstrated experience supporting elite female athletes and/or female teams.
  • Certified Strength & Conditioning Specialist (CSCS), Certified Performance & Sport Scientist (CPSS), or equivalent international certification.
  • Minimum of 3–5 years of experience working in elite sport environments, including professional clubs, collegiate athletics, academies, or national teams.
  • Strong understanding of soccer and the physical demands of the international game.
  • Experience working within multidisciplinary and integrated performance environments.
  • Significant experience with athlete monitoring and performance technologies, including GPS, force plates, athlete management systems, and wellness platforms.
  • Ability to synthesize objective data and translate insights into practical recommendations for players, coaches, and staff.
  • Strong communication, planning, and organizational skills.
  • Capable of working in fast-paced and demanding environments.
  • Must be able to connect “micro” details to the “macro” vision and mission.
  • Proficient experience with Microsoft Suite (Word, PowerPoint, Excel, and Outlook).
  • Ability to work non-traditional hours, including evenings, weekends, and extensive domestic and international travel.
  • Current First Aid and CPR certification.

Desired Qualifications

  • Knowledge of female athlete health, growth and maturation, and long-term athlete development principles.
  • PhD in Sport Science, Exercise Physiology, Kinesiology, or related fields.
  • Experience supporting Youth National Teams, professional clubs, or elite female development pathways.
  • Experience working collaboratively within multidisciplinary teams.
  • Bilingual (English and Spanish).


U.S. Soccer offers a comprehensive compensation package, casual work environment, an inclusive culture, and an atmosphere for professional development.

This policy applies to all our employment practices within our organization. We strongly encourage women, people of color, LGBTQIA, veterans, parents, and persons with disabilities to apply.
job.plain_text_description:
Description
U.S. Soccer Overview
The U.S. Soccer Federation exists in service to soccer. Our aim is to ignite a national passion for the game. Because we believe that soccer is more than a sport; it is a force for good.
We understand the importance and the power of teamwork, on and off the pitch. That is why we work closely with our Federation partners and members, to inspire, support and guide every level of the game: from the grassroots to the National Teams. We want to bring soccer into every home and every community, right across America. Because we believe that soccer can transform lives like no other sport. Soccer can represent the best of U.S.
U.S. Soccer is in a period of significant growth, with ambitious plans for U.S. Soccer in the near and far future. We are, therefore, looking for dynamic servant leaders to join us on this journey: in service to soccer. Applicants must be able to demonstrate visionary leadership, analytical decision-making, professional flexibility, and an empathic management style that builds bold teams and delivers globally significant results.
Position Description
U.S. Soccer is seeking a collaborative and growth-oriented Senior Performance Coach to support the Women’s Youth National Teams. As a member of the Integrated Performance Support (IPS) department, this role will contribute to the delivery and continuous evolution of integrated performance practices through a female lens across camps, competitions, and other player development environments.
Emphasizing that the female lens is at the heart of everything we do, this role aligns with the WNT strategy while integrating an interdisciplinary approach. This position will collaborate closely with Performance Medicine, Performance Nutrition, Performance & Data Analytics, Performance Innovation, and Technical staff to optimize player availability, development, and performance.
The Senior Performance Coach will support the design and implementation of evidence-informed physical preparation strategies, including readiness and load monitoring, physical testing, strength and conditioning, recovery, and performance planning through a female lens. In partnership with coaches and IPS colleagues, this role will help create world-class player experiences that support both team success and long-term player development.
A key focus of this position will be advancing U.S. Soccer’s commitment to becoming world-leading in female health, development, and performance. Working within the Arthur M. Blank National Training Center, the Senior Performance Coach will contribute to the development of integrated systems, innovative practices, and environments that elevate player care across the Women’s Youth National Team pathway.
The ideal candidate is an intellectually curious practitioner and strong teammate who thrives in collaborative, fast-paced environments, embraces innovation, and is passionate about supporting the growth of elite female players.
Primary Responsibilities
Integrated Performance Delivery
- Support the delivery of integrated performance services across the U19-U20 Women’s National Team environments, including domestic and international camps and competitions. - Contribute to the design and implementation of individual and team-based performance strategies that optimize player availability, development, and performance. - Collaborate closely with technical staff on training design, competition preparation, recovery, and long-term player development. - Collaborate with WNT, U23 and other WYNT technical, performance, and medical staff to align club, college, and country communications, facilitate the exchange of information, and promote continuity of player care, to ensure smooth player transitions between club and country environments. - Travel with Youth National Teams to provide on-site performance support.
Female Health & Performance
- Advance U.S. Soccer’s commitment to becoming world-leading in female health, development, and performance. - Support initiatives related to growth and maturation, female health, injury-risk reduction, and long-term player development. - Collaborate with performance medicine, performance nutrition, and technical staff to optimize player readiness and availability.
Physical Preparation & Performance Science
- Support the design and implementation of physical preparation programs (using Teamworks AMS), including strength and conditioning, recovery, and load management strategies. - Oversee player monitoring, physical testing, and performance profiling systems to support evidence-informed decision-making. - Utilize technologies including PlayerData GPS, VALD performance tools, OURA, FitrWoman, Raw Stadia, and a growing portfolio of technologies to support health and performance. - Translate objective performance data into actionable insights for players, coaches, and IPS staff. - Contribute to the ongoing development of best practices in performance science across the women’s pathway.
Integrated Performance Support Collaboration
- Serve as a key member of the Integrated Performance Support (IPS) team, supporting world-class player care and performance services. - Collaborate with Performance Medicine, Performance Nutrition, Performance & Data Analytics, Performance Innovation, and technical staff to support integrated decision-making and player development. - Execute and continuously improve performance methodologies, testing protocols, and operational standards across camps and competitions. - Contribute to a culture of curiosity, collaboration, accountability, and continuous learning. - Support the onboarding and development of network practitioners and interns as needed.
Data, Analytics & Innovation
- Oversee the collection, interpretation, communication, and storage of player performance data in accordance with U.S. Soccer standards. - Partner with analytics and innovation teams to develop and implement novel approaches to player monitoring and decision-making. - Support longitudinal player profiling and talent development initiatives across the Women’s pathway. - Build and maintain relationships with clubs, universities, and external partners to facilitate the exchange of performance information and best practices. - Contribute to the National Training Center as a world-class environment for integrated athlete support, innovation, and organizational learning.
Requirements
Minimum Qualifications
- Master’s degree or higher in Sport Science, Exercise Physiology, Kinesiology, Strength & Conditioning, or related field. - Demonstrated experience supporting elite female athletes and/or female teams. - Certified Strength & Conditioning Specialist (CSCS), Certified Performance & Sport Scientist (CPSS), or equivalent international certification. - Minimum of 3–5 years of experience working in elite sport environments, including professional clubs, collegiate athletics, academies, or national teams. - Strong understanding of soccer and the physical demands of the international game. - Experience working within multidisciplinary and integrated performance environments. - Significant experience with athlete monitoring and performance technologies, including GPS, force plates, athlete management systems, and wellness platforms. - Ability to synthesize objective data and translate insights into practical recommendations for players, coaches, and staff. - Strong communication, planning, and organizational skills. - Capable of working in fast-paced and demanding environments. - Must be able to connect “micro” details to the “macro” vision and mission. - Proficient experience with Microsoft Suite (Word, PowerPoint, Excel, and Outlook). - Ability to work non-traditional hours, including evenings, weekends, and extensive domestic and international travel. - Current First Aid and CPR certification.
Desired Qualifications
- Knowledge of female athlete health, growth and maturation, and long-term athlete development principles. - PhD in Sport Science, Exercise Physiology, Kinesiology, or related fields. - Experience supporting Youth National Teams, professional clubs, or elite female development pathways. - Experience working collaboratively within multidisciplinary teams. - Bilingual (English and Spanish).
